results.title: Design for Equitable Communities—Framework for Design Excellence
results.content: Good design positively impacts the future by helping communities thrive—socially, economically, and environmentally. ## Design for Equitable Communities. Social vulnerability refers to the potential negative effects on communities caused by external stresses on human health. Architects can address social vulnerability by designing better housing, public functions, supportive programming, green areas and open space, and socially connected communities. Architects must listen to community members, learn from their localized expertise, and provide responsive design solutions in order to establish a viable, enduring project that enhances the community. Equitable resilience means designing to meet life-sustaining needs and passive survivability for everyone in the community. Howard Brown Health’s Broadway Youth Center provides affirming health care, human services, and community support for LGBTQ+ youth ages 12–24. Near multiple transit lines, it serves vulnerable communities with trauma-informed design that fosters safety, belonging, and empowerment. 2023 AIA ARCHITECTURE AWARD RECIPIENT LUBBER RUN COMMUNITY CENTER, ARLINGTON, VA., VMDO ARCHITECTS. Invest in the next generation of designers and the diverse communities they serve.
